entries.title: Reflections on Wave-Particle Duality and Modern Physics
entries.body: Studying Unit 1 helped me realize how classical physics fails to explain atomic-scale phenomena like blackbody radiation and the photoelectric effect. Understanding that light and moving particles exhibit both wave and particle characteristics was initially confusing, but breaking down key experiments—like the double-slit experiment and Compton scattering—helped bridge the gap. I still need to practice applying the formulas for Wien's displacement law and Heisenberg's uncertainty principle to numerical problems, but I feel much more confident about the core conceptual shifts in modern physics.

entries.title: Reflection on Waves & Simple Harmonic Motion
entries.body:
In Unit 2, I developed a solid understanding of fundamental wave behaviors and oscillations. I learned how simple harmonic motion is driven by a restoring force that brings a body back toward equilibrium, and how energy and momentum transfer through progressive waves without permanently displacing the medium. I also explored key phenomena like wave interference and beats resulting from slightly differing frequencies.

The trickiest part of this unit was distinguishing clearly between energy transfer mechanisms, such as power versus intensity, as well as visualizing phase differences in SHM. To master these concepts, I drew comparison tables and worked through visual wave diagrams. Moving forward, I can apply these principles when studying sound synthesis, optics, and architectural acoustics.

entries.title: Reflection on Wave Optics & Lasers
entries.body:
In Unit 4, I explored the fascinating wave nature of light through polarization, diffraction, and interference. I learned how constructive and destructive interference alter wave amplitudes, and how the bending of light around obstacles creates diffraction patterns governed by grating elements. Additionally, I studied the principles behind lasers, focusing on stimulated emission and how light amplification produces monochromatic, coherent, and unidirectional beams. Finally, I examined polarization, understanding how unpolarized light becomes polarized and how Brewster's law connects the tangent of the polarization angle to the refractive index of a denser medium.

The most challenging part of this unit was visualizing how path differences in interference grating setups lead to specific diffraction maxima. To overcome this, I drew out ray diagrams and stepped through the derivations linking grating elements to wave angles. Moving forward, I can apply these optical principles to fields like fiber-optic communications, laser technology, and precision metrology.

entries.title: Mechanics
entries.body:
In this unit, I built a solid foundation in mechanics by exploring how and why objects move. I examined the core principles of kinematics, studied different types of friction (including the laws of friction and angle of repose), and understood the dynamics of reference frames. Furthermore, I dived into momentum, impulse, and the work-energy theorem, connecting theoretical laws like conservation of momentum to practical applications like spring-mass systems and motion against gravity.

What was difficult?

Some of the initial challenges involved distinguishing between inertial and non-inertial reference frames and visualizing the nuanced forces acting on an object at an angle of limiting friction. Working through complex problems involving impulse-momentum changes and energy conservation also required careful attention to detail and units.

How did I overcome it?

I overcame these hurdles by breaking down each law into its core components, reviewing real-world applications, and organizing my notes systematically. Writing down precise definitions and revisiting the underlying equations helped clarify how different mechanical forces interact in a given system.

Where can I apply this knowledge?

This understanding of mechanics is essential not only for advanced physics problems but also for everyday engineering and motion analysis. Whether it is calculating forces in structural design, understanding vehicle safety dynamics (like airbags and momentum changes), or analyzing simple harmonic motion, these concepts provide a critical analytical framework for solving physical problems.
